headline: IVANHOE ELECTRIC RELEASES ARIZONA COPPER PFS — 23-Year Mine, $1.9B NPV, Cathode Without Smelting; $1.1B EXIM Backing
snippet: Ivanhoe Electric Inc. (NYSE/TSX: IE) released its 2026 Preliminary Feasibility Study for the Santa Cruz Copper Project in Arizona on September 23, defining a 23-year underground mine producing 72,000 tonnes of copper cathode annually via heap leach and SX-EW — no smelting required. The 2025 base-case NPV was $1.9 billion at a 24% IRR at then-current copper prices; with COMEX copper now at $6.75/lb versus the prior study's $4.83/lb sensitivity, economics are materially stronger. The 2026 update incorporates a Robbins Crossover XRE tunnel boring machine for underground access, revising capex and schedule. The Export-Import Bank of the United States issued a Preliminary Project Letter for $1.1 billion in potential debt financing, a key de-risking milestone ahead of a projected 2028 first production at what would be the largest new copper mine permitted on US soil in a generation.

headline: GOLIATH WRAPS SUREBET — 48,443m in 94 Days, 100% Hit Rate, 2.01 km² Footprint; Best: 13.81 g/t Au Over 4.85m
snippet: Goliath Resources Ltd. (TSXV: GOT) completed its 2026 drill campaign at the Surebet Discovery on the Golddigger Property in BC's Golden Triangle — 48,443 metres across 97 holes drilled in just 94 days, with visible gold in 52 of 92 holes and a 100% hit rate across all holes ever drilled at the system. Best intercept: 13.81 g/t gold over 4.85 metres (Golden Gate Zone); also 9.12 g/t AuEq over 11.27m and 31.42 g/t AuEq over a 1.0m sub-interval. The Surebet footprint expanded 12% to 2.01 km², with the Bonanza Zone up 19% to 1.51 km² and Golden Gate up 38% to 1.17 km². Goliath has now drilled over 200,000 cumulative metres at Surebet since 2021 without a single blank hole — a statistic that sets up a maiden resource estimate as the next major catalyst.

headline: CHINA GOLD IMPORTS BREAK RECORDS — 1,000+ Tonnes Through August, Surpassing Full-Year 2025 as Price Holds $4,399/oz
snippet: China's gold purchases through August 2026 exceeded 1,000 tonnes, surpassing the nation's total imports for all of 2025 — providing the structural demand floor that has kept gold futures at $4,399/oz on September 22–23 despite Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations climbing toward 70%. Gold is now up just 0.7% in 2026 but trades 25% higher year-over-year, with the January record close of $5,419/oz remaining the ceiling. For junior gold exploration companies, the sustained Chinese institutional and retail demand — driven by currency anxiety and a structural shift away from real estate as a savings vehicle — represents a demand-side support that is likely to outlast the current Fed tightening cycle.

headline: 166 g/t GOLD AND 3,383 g/t SILVER IN 3.1m — Cambria Hits Bonanza at BC's Premier-Northern Light Deposit
snippet: Cambria Gold Mines Inc. (TSXV: CAMB; OTCQX: CAMVF) reported 166.22 g/t Au and 3,383 g/t Ag over 3.1 metres in hole P26U-0095, including a 1.1-metre bonanza core of 467 g/t Au and 9,510 g/t Ag, from the Prew Zone of the Premier-Northern Light Deposit near Stewart, BC — one of Canada's highest-grade historic gold-silver districts. Results are from 6,923 metres in 70 surface and underground drillholes across the ongoing 2026 infill campaign. The northeastern Prew Zone is defining a high-grade silver-gold corridor associated with silver sulphosalts and native silver/electrum, suggesting a distinct mineralizing event capable of hosting significant bonanza intervals beyond the current resource outline.

headline: AYA GOLD & SILVER HITS 593 g/t AgEq OVER 15.2m at Boumadine — 145,719m Drilled; Three Zones All Open in Morocco
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX: AYA) released fresh high-grade infill results from its Boumadine Project in Morocco, headlined by BOU-DD26-883 intersecting 593 g/t AgEq over 15.2 metres — including 1,038 g/t AgEq over 4.2m — from the Main Trend, and BOU-DD26-848 returning 392 g/t AgEq over 24.3 metres. The 2026 campaign now totals 145,719 metres across 406 diamond drill holes, with the Main Trend extending 5.4 km, the Tizi Zone 2.0 km and the Imariren Zone 1.2 km — all open in all directions. Aya operates the producing Zgounder Silver Mine in Morocco and is systematically building Boumadine toward a standalone development decision, with results confirming high-grade continuity that supports further resource growth.

headline: COPPER GIANT INTERSECTS 804m AT 0.56% CuEq at Colombia's Mocoa — High-Grade Core 103m of 1.07% CuEq; PEA Due Q4
snippet: Copper Giant Resources Corp. reported that infill daughter hole MD-073 at the Mocoa copper-molybdenum porphyry in Putumayo, Colombia returned 804 metres at 0.56% CuEq*, including a 103-metre high-grade core averaging 1.07% CuEq* (0.57% Cu, 0.095% Mo) — the third directional daughter hole from the MD-064 platform, delivering nearly 7,000 metres of drilling from a single pad without new road access. Mocoa hosts an Inferred resource of 12.7 billion pounds copper-equivalent across 1.12 billion tonnes. A fourth drill rig is being positioned on the western flank where the porphyry system remains undefined, with a Preliminary Economic Assessment targeted for Q4 2026. At $6.75/lb copper, the timing of this PEA release would coincide with the strongest copper pricing environment in the project's history.

headline: SILVER HITS WEEKLY HIGH BEFORE US-CHINA SUMMIT — Sixth Straight Deficit Year, 800-Tonne Chinese Monthly Imports Back $67/oz
snippet: Silver December futures touched $67.32/oz on September 22 — the highest level since September 9 — as markets positioned ahead of Thursday's US-China summit, where a partial reversal of rare earth and critical mineral export controls could be announced. Silver is up 59% year-over-year and the Silver Institute's 2026 World Silver Survey confirmed a sixth consecutive structural deficit year, with the cumulative shortfall since 2021 approaching 800 million ounces. Chinese monthly imports topped 800 tonnes in March 2026, more than double any prior record, driven by solar manufacturers and retail investors priced out of gold. For silver equity investors, the combination of structural deficit, Chinese restocking demand and potential summit catalysts represents a rare alignment of fundamental tailwinds.

headline: GREENLAND SECURITY PACT RESHAPES RARE EARTH RACE — Chinese Investment Locked Out; Tanbreez and Sarfartoq in Strategic Focus
snippet: A US-Denmark-Greenland security agreement announced September 21 bars any US-adversary nation from making "sensitive investments" in Greenland without US written approval — effectively excluding Chinese capital from the island's substantial rare earth and critical mineral resource base. Critical Metals Corp. (CRML), which holds the Tanbreez rare-earth project in southern Greenland, surged 43% Monday before giving back 6% Tuesday on profit-taking, retaining a 23% monthly gain. The pact follows the Greenland Mines acquisition of the Sarfartoq Nd-Pr rare earths project for $35 million earlier this month. With China controlling ~70% of global rare earth mining and ~90% of magnet production, a geopolitically secured Greenland supply corridor represents a structurally new variable for Western defense and EV supply chains — and for investors in listed North Atlantic rare earth plays.

headline: REVIVAL GOLD NOW 64% THROUGH MERCUR INFILL — Utah Heap-Leach Developer Posts 1.82 g/t Au Over 29m; PFS Due Q1 2027
snippet: Revival Gold Inc. (TSXV: RVG; OTCQX: RVLGF) reported that its 2026 infill drill program at the Mercur Gold Project in Utah is 64% complete with 11,600 metres drilled in 119 reverse circulation and core holes, headlined by 1.82 g/t Au over 29.0 metres and 0.92 g/t Au over 33.5 metres in the Main Mercur area. The program is converting Inferred resources to Measured and Indicated categories ahead of a Preliminary Feasibility Study targeted for Q1 2027. Results to date continue to support the grade and leachability assumptions from the company's 2025 PEA. Mercur is a Carlin-trend-style heap-leachable gold deposit on permitted ground in Utah's Tooele County — a fully permitted, road-accessible heap-leach project at a point in the cycle where the barrier to project financing is economics, not permitting.

headline: COPPER TARIFF CLOCK IS RUNNING — Section 232 Sets 15% From Jan 2027, 30% From 2028; Decision Window Now Open
snippet: With the Commerce Department's June 2026 copper market update now completed, the White House can formally impose Section 232 national security tariffs on refined copper imports: 15% from January 2027 and 30% from 2028, per the recommended phased schedule. A 50% tariff on semi-finished copper products is already in effect since August 2025. The tariff cycle is one of two factors — alongside Chinese supply cuts — driving COMEX copper to $6.75/lb and toward its $6.89/lb all-time record. For North American copper developers and producers, domestic tariff protection at a time of record prices creates the most compelling project-financing environment for permitted US copper projects in at least two decades.

headline: THE $96 URANIUM TERM PRICE PUZZLE — Why Are Mining Stocks Lagging Record Contract Prices?
snippet: Uranium's long-term contract price hit a nominal all-time record of US$96.50/lb in September 2026 — surpassing the 2007 peak of $95/lb — as Kazatomprom slashed 8 million pounds from its 2026 production guidance, reset its 100% nominal output level downward, and withdrew multi-year forward guidance entirely. Spot uranium trades around $89.70/lb. Yet uranium mining equities have broadly underperformed the commodity itself, with the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index up 17% in September compared to a larger move in term prices. Crux Investor examines whether the equity lag reflects rational risk pricing or a lagging recognition opportunity — an important distinction for retail investors building positions in uranium developers and explorers ahead of what Cameco, Kazatomprom and Sprott are projecting as a structurally tight market through the decade.
